faq.q: Where do the over-$1.8M listings on this page actually sit?
faq.a: Across the whole community, not in one neighbourhood: the cards visible at reading were labelled Grandview (3), Elgin Chantrell (2), Morgan Creek (1) and White Rock (1) — the page is a price band over all nine S Surrey White Rock sub-areas, crossing the Surrey/White Rock municipal boundary.

faq.q: What extra checks matter at this price level?
faq.a: The ones the page's own guide copy names — zoning, Agricultural Land Reserve status, wells and septic, and floodplain rules. ALR status is confirmed with the Agricultural Land Commission (its housing frame allows one principal residence up to 500 m² plus one additional residence of 90 m² or 186 m² depending on parcel size), not from a note on title.

faq.q: Can an acreage home in South Surrey have a suite or coach house?
faq.a: Under Surrey's current rules, one secondary suite is permitted in a single family dwelling, capped at 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable area, and a coach house or garden suite runs 35–75 m², up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots where the principal dwelling has not used its maximum floor area; the old 90 m² suite cap is not a current rule (~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/rules-gaps-2026-11-01.md, read 2026-11-01).

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in South Surrey?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in South Surrey?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.
